findings.reason: a node that tests only store-against-store will land a read-back that never meets the observed fault, declare the section done, and the loss will recur at the next promotion that commits over a plan write the way the evidence describes.
findings.text: the done-when interleaves a promotion's store write with each of six store writes, but the store already performs the check-and-replace as one step under a per-plan path lock (reckon/_store.py:400-428) and re-reads the file's version inside that lock, raising VersionConflict for a stale expected_version (reckon/_store.py:1750), so "both changes are in the file at the end, or the later writer is refused naming the version conflict" holds before any change and the test passes on the unfixed code; the negative control's "with that read-back removed and the promotion writing from its earlier read" cannot produce the stated loss either, because the in-lock version check still refuses the stale write, and a read-back that reports not-landed after another writer erased the change is not the refusal naming a version conflict the section requires — meanwhile the Why's own evidence names a promotion that committed the plan file at 07:54:20 UTC and left it reading version 1102 with the declarations absent, which is the signature of a git-level write of the plan file that no store lock or store read-back coordinates
